t.1.162.1: The Gandharva said: Having spoken thus, the blameless one then swiftly went upward; but the king fell down once more upon the ground right there.
t.1.162.3: For, seeing that great archer fallen to the ground, bereft of his horses, his minister became as if set ablaze by fire.
t.1.162.2: The minister, with his retinue, saw him in the great forest, fallen upon the ground like Śakra's banner raised high at its appointed time.
t.1.162.4: Approaching him in haste, alarmed out of affection, he raised up that king, who lay stupefied by desire.
t.1.162.5: Like a father lifting his fallen son, he raised the lord of kings from the ground, he who was elder in wisdom and in age, in fame and in self-restraint.
t.1.162.6: The minister raised him up and was freed from his anxiety, and to him, now risen, he spoke with gentle and sweet words: "Do not be afraid, tiger among men, and may good fortune be yours, sinless one."
t.1.162.7: He made out that king, worn out by hunger and thirst, lying fallen on the surface of the earth, he who in battle was the feller of his foes.
t.1.162.9: Then the mighty king, his breath restored, dismissed that entire army, all except that one minister.
t.1.162.8: Then he sprinkled his head with very cool water, fragrant as the lotus, and touched the crown of the king.
t.1.162.10: Then, at the command of that king, the great army departed, but the king himself sat down again on that mountain plateau.
t.1.162.11: Then on that finest of mountains, having purified himself and joining his palms in reverence, he stood upon the ground with arms raised high, longing to win the favor of Sūrya.
t.1.162.12: Then King Saṃvaraṇa, the slayer of enemies, went in his mind to Vasiṣṭha, the best of seers, his family priest.
t.1.162.13: Then, while that lord of men remained fixed in one place night and day, the brahmin seer came to him on the twelfth day.
t.1.162.14: That great seer, whose self was perfected, knowing by divine means and thus understanding that the king's mind had been stolen away by Tapatī,
t.1.162.15: Then that righteous one addressed that best of kings, who was thus self-controlled, desiring to accomplish that very king's purpose.
t.1.162.16: While that lord of men looked on, the blessed seer, radiant as the sun, strode upward to behold the sun.
t.1.162.17: Then the brahmin, approaching the thousand-rayed Sun with joined palms, joyfully made himself known to him, saying, "I am Vasiṣṭha."
t.1.162.18: The greatly radiant Vivasvān said to that best of sages: "Great ṛṣi, may you be welcome! Tell me what you wish."
